web_links.about: No web addresses or links in a reply (operator 2026-10-06: "no urls" - gemma2:2b made up addresses and handles, and the other Brobot repeated them). Before a reply is shown or spoken, a link (http://, https://, www.) or a bare web address is taken out, unless it holds keep_with - then only the bare address stays (crushn8r.ca, said by the pronunciation registry as "Crush-Ehnaydir dot see-aye"). gopodDropWebLinks, gopod_kgsim_response_shaping.go.

stretched_words.about: A stretched word is said stretched, not spelled out (operator 2026-10-06: "Long 'brooooo' = 'bro-o-o'"): a word ending in one vowel repeated min_repeat or more times is spoken with that vowel said_repeats times, joined by hyphens - brooooo -> bro-o-o, gooooo -> go-o-o. Speech only; the bubble shows it as written. gopodSayStretchedWords, gopod_pronunciation.go.

merged_words.about: Merged words get a hyphen before they're spoken (operator 2026-10-06: "snoozefest = snooze-fest ... a filter to catch merged words ... and auto-split"). Only poetically licensed, made-up merges are split (operator 2026-10-06: "split poetically licensed/composed words, not recognized doublewords"): a word of min_letters or more that isn't in the dictionaries, and splits cleanly into two dictionary words of min_part letters or more, is spoken split: snoozefest -> snooze-fest. A dictionary word plus one of word_endings (robotically = robotic + ally), or a dropped g (somethin), is a real word and stays whole. With several splits, the most even one wins, then the longer second part (kickstart -> kick-start, not kicks-tart). Speech only; the bubble shows the word as written. Words in the pronunciation registry and keep_whole count as known words (with their endings: rockstars) and are never split; a real compound the dictionaries miss goes in keep_whole. dictionaries: the system word list plus aspell's expanded English list (made once with: aspell -l en dump master | aspell -l en expand). A missing file is skipped; none at all = no splitting.

spoken_symbols.about: How a symbol is said (operator 2026-10-08: "add the missing symbols, the old 'times' and 'divided by', and the LaTeX cleanup to the speech cleanup"; "$" = "dollars"). Speech only - the bubble keeps the symbol. "$5" is said "5 dollars". LaTeX math (\frac{1}{2}, \overline{3}, \( \)) is cleaned first: a fraction becomes 1/2, an overline "3 repeating" (gopod_spoken_symbols.go).
spoken_symbols.show_as_said_about: 2026-10-27 (operator: "2026 * should be observed as 20 26 * spoken & heard, highlights follow 20 26 spoken/heard pattern"): spoken forms a Brobot's bubble shows the way they're said - years: a date's year as its two halves (October 27, 20 26), like gopodSpeakYears says it.

llm.about: The Brobots' LLM stays warm (operator 2026-10-03: "I prefer a pre-warm up and then have it stay loaded, so it doesn't go cold"). At Wire-Pod start one silent request loads the model (same model and endpoint as the chat); warmup_text shows on the page meanwhile and disappears when done. Then every refresh_seconds Ollama is told to keep the model loaded for keep_alive (a negative value = until Ollama stops). Nothing is spoken or kept in the chat. A song with "llm_warmup": true in its knobs.json (the Bingo test) shows the same bubble at the start of a live run, for at least song_warmup_min_seconds or until its warm request is done (operator 2026-10-04). 2026-10-04 (operator: "make it like a horizontal battery power level indicator ... left to right, red to green, cold llm to fully warmed up llm ... message changes, LLM Warming Up to LLM Ready ... use same hour glass"): the bubble is a battery of leds LEDs, red to green, filling over expected_seconds (the cold load takes about 2 minutes here) but never full until the model is loaded; then all green with ready_text, the hourglass settled - and the bubble stays in the window, saved with the chat (operator: "it is to stay. Keep it in"). The rattle countdown keeps its Bingo balls. warmup_done_text (operator 2026-10-09; 2026-10-10 "Combine into one bubble"): the start's warm-up bubble reads "LLM Ready. Warm-up complete.", and Goverlord says both.
llm.opener_about: GOLDEN opener template (operator 2026-10-16, his exact lines, one line each message: 1: "(music) Voice files generation check." - 2: "Voice files generated. Language Model Loading" - 3: "Language Model Loaded, Master CrushN8r. Your move. (music)"; "visual: ensure bubble is fully rendered/loaded (off screen) * audio: ensure audio fully loaded & playable * upon both audio/visual and no sooner, position bubble correct & proper in chat window"). Message 1 (voices_text) shows at every start - it is the check; message 2 (warmup_text; wait_text empty, nothing added); message 3 (ready_text; warmup_done_text empty). A song run: message 2, then run_ready_text, the song's own llm_ready_text (its knobs) and run_ready_end, a line each. (music) is shown, for deaf viewers, where the stings play; the butler doesn't say it. 2026-10-16 (operator: "remove 1st \"(music)\" & remove its audio play ... Keep: \"Language Model Loaded, Master CrushN8r. Your move. (music)\" + audio play"): message 1 is "Voice files generation check.", no sting; the end sting stays. Locked by TestWarmupSequenceGolden.

llm.warmup_text: Voice files generated. Language Model Loading

Sequential Run Check"): one System llm bubble from the start, its message in turn: voices_text + wait_text while the voices are made, warmup_text + wait_text while the LLM warms (skipped when warm), wait_text while the lines in between play, then the ready line.
llm.warmup_check_seconds_about: 2026-10-13 (operator: "'LLM Warming up.' not included in message update"): the LLM Warming Up step always shows; a model already warm holds it this long (no voice), a cold one until it's loaded.
llm.temperature_about: 2026-10-07 (operator: "a brobots creativity-temperature (as-is = default setting) ... for segments requiring a say-it-flat like scripted stuff"): the Brobots' creativity per reply - temperature (1, Wire-Pod's as-is) for a normal question, say_line_temperature for a question whose value point has a scripted line (value_points.say_lines). The scripted line itself is said by the code, flat; this only steadies the LLM's talk around it, where facts were invented. One temperature per reply: it can't change partway through.

llm.run_ready_text_about: 2026-10-14 (operator: "part 1 standard * keep it in settings file once * each song gives only part 2"): a run's LLM Ready message is this, then the run's own part 2 - a song's knobs.json llm_ready_text, the interview's interview_script.llm_ready_text ("We here, are Fart Joke Ready"). answer_chains_about: GOLDEN thought bubbles template - the answer chain (operator 2026-10-21: "build the thought bubbles boilerplate template * start with a base scaffolding for answer chain * copy scaffolding template & cater to different response groups * you can now apply to gomad responses, and some system responses"). base is the scaffold; each group is {"from": "base"} (a copy) or its own parts. Stitch parts add to the answer - start_snippet (before), weather_kit, end_snippet, redirect (after), in order around llm. Answer parts are the answer and end the chain when they apply - who_line, manager_take, llm. A part that doesn't apply this time is skipped. Groups: brobots (a Brobot's answer), brobots_follow_up (the second Brobot in a line to both), gomad_persona (a line to CHALK or PLAYHEAD). gopod_answer_chain.go.

A single answer: report, comment, value point, reminders (brobots). Each Brobot's own unit and clock (his robot settings: Brobot 2 F / 12-hour, Brobot 1 C / 24-hour). The model's parts: chain_prompts.

reply_tighten.about: Tighter replies (operator 2026-10-06: "Tighten the responses"; 2026-10-07: a response budget instead of one cap - "Can you hear me? vs Tell me all about yourself"; gopod_reply_tighten.go). On the LLM's part of a reply only, before the scripted lines go in. The budget is worked out by the code per question, the prompt is unchanged: base_sentences, plus per_topic_sentences for each topic the question loads (topic_sentences sets a topic's own number - checks, "can you hear me?", adds none), plus more_sentences when it has a more_words phrase, never over max_sentences; after a point's scripted line (value_points.say_lines) the LLM gets say_line_sentences (2026-10-07: its talk after the line argued with it). Anything in [square brackets] is dropped - a placeholder, never speech. not_sentence_ends don't end a sentence. drop_lists cuts numbered and bulleted list lines and ``` blocks and keeps **bold** words without the stars; drop_stage_directions cuts *stage directions* (two words or more, or one on stage_directions.json) - false brings back the stage_direction_emojis lines.
reply_tighten.budget_off_about: 2026-10-08 (operator: "I like this: 'It's like he took all these tricky bits... and made them into something beautiful.' * remove 2-sentence clamps & stuff"): true - no reply is cut to a sentence count (the budget below and say_line_sentences are kept, unused); the prompt's own sizing and the clean-up (brackets, drop_sentences_with, lists, stage directions) stay. false brings the budget back.
reply_tighten.free_max_sentences_about: 2026-10-24 (operator: "Brobot 1 response * is amazing, lol, but too long"): a free answer (no value point - a greeting too) keeps at most this many sentences, budget_off or not.
